question: A lathi (bamboo staff) and a stone are examples of which class of weapons in the forensic classification of weapons of medicolegal importance?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Blunt weapons (lathi, stone, iron rod, cricket bat, fist) act by concentrating force over a broad contact surface, producing contusions and lacerations. They contrast with sharp-edged weapons (knife, sword) that cut, sharp-pointed weapons (awl, needle) that penetrate, and combined weapons (bayonet, dagger) that both cut and penetrate.

Incorrect. Sharp-edged weapons (e.g., knife, sickle, sword) have a fine cutting edge and produce incised wounds with clean margins. A lathi and a stone lack cutting edges — they produce injuries by blunt impact.
Incorrect. Combined weapons (e.g., bayonet, dagger with a pointed tip and an edge) can both penetrate and cut. A lathi and a stone have neither a point nor an edge — they are purely blunt weapons.
Incorrect. Sharp-pointed weapons (e.g., awl, needle, pointed nail) produce penetrating puncture wounds due to their point. A lathi and a stone lack any pointed configuration.

overallFeedback.feedback: The four weapon classes in FM forensic classification: Blunt (lathi, stone, fist), Sharp-edged (knife, sword), Sharp-pointed (awl, needle), Combined (bayonet, dagger). Lathi and stone = blunt.
Correct. Blunt weapons → contusions and lacerations. This is the most common class in Indian assault cases involving domestic objects.
